case_number: CIVIL APPEAL NO. OF 2024 [@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) NO. OF 2024]
summary: The appeal challenges the Gauhati High Court's dismissal of a writ petition that sought to quash a Foreigners Tribunal order declaring the appellant a foreigner. The Tribunal had held the appellant failed to discharge the burden of proving he was not a foreigner under Section 9 of the Foreigners Act, 1946. The appellant argued he suffered from serious health issues preventing timely appearance, was denied a fair hearing, and that discrepancies in documents were minor (e.g., spelling, date of birth). The State justified the burden of proof on the alleged foreigner, citing threats from illegal migration and precedents like Sarbananda Sonowal I. Despite prior directions for a fresh hearing, the Tribunal reaffirmed its foreigner declaration. The appellant contended this was perverse given his familial and residential ties in India.
legal_provisions_cited: Sarbananda Sonowal v Union of India, (2005) 5 SCC 665
Abdul Kuddus v Union of India, (2019) 6 SCC 604
